A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, behavioral experiment, models, and main analyses. All pages, figures, tables, and the supplementary material added in v2 are readable; v1 ends with references.

before.justification: v1 reports original results from 72 participants, model predictions of grouping judgments and reaction times, object-centricity analyses, and Gram-alignment experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds behavioral analyses, linear-readout and CLS-distillation controls, and condition-specific model–human correlations.

M1.justification: The proposed patch-feature readout, object-centricity analysis, and Gram-alignment procedure are retained. Section 6.2 newly documents architecture and training details without establishing a changed method; linear readout and CLS distillation are additional comparison methods.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same COCO2017-based grouping and reaction-time tasks, 72 participants, 255 experimental images, and 1,020 behavioral trials, alongside ImageNet training. The supplementary analyses examine this retained coverage rather than introducing another dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: The nine main backbones remain unchanged. Sections 6.2–6.3 add focused comparators: linear RT readouts across all nine models, CLS-token distillation for IN21k and IN1K ViT B, and fine-tuning without Gram loss for the ImageNet-accuracy comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 revises the stated 10-fold RT protocol to nested validation, adding an inner 90/10 training–validation split for early stopping and hyperparameter selection. Table 1 also changes DINO ViT B's large-dataset designation from Yes to No. These reported revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun or a different checkpoint was evaluated.

E4.justification: New supplementary analyses examine subject and condition accuracy, sensitivity, response bias, RT-distribution separation, and directional consistency. Linear-readout and CLS-distillation controls test alternative explanations for alignment, while Figure 8 and Table 2 examine correlations within each condition. These substantially expand validation beyond v1's retained layer/head and Gram-alignment analyses.

E5.justification: v2 adds significance reporting for the cross-model association and supplementary analyses, subject-level dispersion statistics, and the noise ceiling's standard deviation of 0.037. The existing 10 seeds per fold and 20 subject splits remain unchanged; no increase in repetitions is established.

E6.justification: Table 1's grouping accuracies and the main plotted results are retained, but substantial supplementary findings are added. These include linear-readout association r=0.917, condition-specific correlations, raw model–human correlations, and behavioral sensitivity/bias results. CLS distillation yields 0.59→0.59 and 0.59→0.58 for the two ViTs, compared with Gram alignment's 0.59→0.72 and 0.59→0.70. These are additional comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the stated ROC definitions: fractions of active patches falling inside/outside an object become threshold-positive fractions among within-/outside-object patches. This is a mathematical-definition correction; the displayed ROC results and Gram-matrix mathematics are retained, and neither version supplies formal proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction restricts the claim that training objective outweighs architecture to the evaluated model set and acknowledges that these factors are not fully decoupled. The conclusion similarly replaces 'matters more' with 'a major factor beyond architecture alone.' The central benchmark, object-centricity, and Gram-alignment contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges architecture/objective confounding and adds interpretations addressing readout capacity, global teacher distillation, classification performance, response bias, and condition-specific effects. The conclusion also moderates its characterization of patch correlations as a fundamental organizing principle to an important contributor.

D1.justification: Section 6.2 supplies previously missing feature dimensions, readout architecture, losses, optimizers, learning rates, schedules, epochs, gradient accumulation, and training-only RT normalization. It specifies last-block-only Gram fine-tuning and classification/Gram loss weights of 1/10. The abstract adds a code/data access link; its external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chen et al.'s 'Unsupervised segmentation in real-world images via Spelke object inference' to the introductory positioning. The related-work narrative otherwise remains substantially unchanged; publication and bibliographic updates to retained references do not represent additional research coverage.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. Changes include localized clarification of validation, normalization, ROC definitions, and Gram similarity; qualified claims; supplementary cross-references; keywords and affiliation edits; and a new supplementary section organized into three subsections.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the document with a narrower text area, running headers, resized and repositioned figures, and wrapped Table 1 headings. It adds the four-panel Figure 8 and Tables 2–3, while retaining the main figure content. This is a substantial layout revision beyond pagination changes.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited controls and missing reproducibility information. The supplementary readout and distillation comparisons strengthen assessment of the central mechanism, while behavioral checks, raw correlations, and detailed training specifications make the evidence easier to evaluate and reproduce. Corrected ROC definitions and narrower architecture/objective claims improve precision. These gains concern evidential support and transparency, rather than higher headline performance.
